scope_status: Independent discovery from supplied brief only; exact plan not yet released.

sources.title: ISO 1996-1:2016, Acoustics — Description, measurement and assessment of environmental noise — Part 1: Basic quantities and assessment procedures
sources.version_or_commit: Edition 3, 2016-03; official ISO record said last reviewed and confirmed in 2021 and current at access.
sources.locator: Official ISO abstract and lifecycle/status, especially lines 22-25 and 43-51 of the page.
sources.observed_operation: Defines community-noise quantities and assessment. Long-term community-annoyance guidance is limited to residential areas/long-term uses; recognizes low-frequency, tonal, and impulsive features when authorities consider them; requires the physical quantity be named; does not specify environmental-noise limits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Metric and assessment context must be selected; same measured dB can represent different underlying quantities. Special character corrections are discretionary where authorities deem necessary. No default local limit is supplied.
sources.applicability: Supports defining the neighbor's desired outcome/metric and avoiding invented thresholds. Long-term annoyance guidance is not a direct prediction for intermittent music at this unspecified courtyard.

sources.title: ISO 1996-2:2017, Acoustics — Description, measurement and assessment of environmental noise — Part 2: Determination of sound pressure levels
sources.version_or_commit: Edition 3, 2017-07; official ISO record said last reviewed/confirmed in 2026 and current at access.
sources.locator: Official ISO abstract and lifecycle/status, especially lines 22-24 and 43-64.
sources.observed_operation: Describes direct measurement and calculation-based extrapolation of outdoor environmental sound pressure levels; gives some indoor guidance; measurement effort determines uncertainty, which is to be determined and reported.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Primarily outdoor use; no maximum allowable uncertainty is prescribed, so the user chooses effort and reports resulting uncertainty.
sources.applicability: Useful framework for courtyard measurement and comparing scenarios after an outcome/metric is agreed. It does not supply this project's limit or establish a causal path.

sources.title: ISO 16283-1:2014, Acoustics — Field measurement of sound insulation in buildings and of building elements — Part 1: Airborne sound insulation
sources.version_or_commit: Edition 1, 2014-02 plus Amendment 1 (2017); official ISO record confirmed the base edition in 2025 and current at access.
sources.locator: Official ISO scope/status/edition and amendment listing, especially lines 22-25, 48-51, 60-89.
sources.observed_operation: Uses sound-pressure measurements for airborne insulation between rooms; scope 10–250 m³ and 50–5000 Hz; results can apply to furnished or unfurnished rooms with diffuse or non-diffuse fields and be frequency dependent.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Only airborne room-to-room insulation within its specified range. Amendment 1:2017 is listed; the abstract accessed did not expose the amendment text.
sources.applicability: A later acoustician-led option if source and receiver rooms/access/geometry are known. It is not a general courtyard disturbance metric and cannot by itself identify structure-borne contribution.

sources.title: ISO 16283-3:2016, Acoustics — Field measurement of sound insulation in buildings and of building elements — Part 3: Façade sound insulation
sources.version_or_commit: Edition 1, 2016-02; official ISO record showed Published / stage 90.92 (to be revised) at access; no replacement was identified in the record.
sources.locator: Official ISO abstract, edition, and lifecycle/status, lines 45-62 and 90-96.
sources.observed_operation: Specifies sound-pressure procedures for airborne façade-element or whole-façade insulation, 10–250 m³ rooms and 50–5000 Hz; results can address diffuse and non-diffuse fields.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Airborne facade measurement only; published 2016 edition is marked for revision, so verify lifecycle before a formal commissioned test.
sources.applicability: Potential later method for a characterized facade and room. It does not determine ground-borne transfer or the relevant neighborhood response.

sources.title: ISO 12354-1:2017, Building acoustics — Estimation of acoustic performance of buildings from the performance of elements — Part 1: Airborne sound insulation between rooms
sources.version_or_commit: Edition 1, 2017-07; official ISO record showed confirmed in 2023, published and to be revised in the 2026 record.
sources.locator: Official ISO abstract/scope and lifecycle, especially lines 22-23 and 46-52.
sources.observed_operation: Calculation models use measured element data for direct/indirect flanking paths plus theory for structural-element propagation; detailed bands cover 100–3150 Hz and may extend to 50 Hz if element and junction data are available.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Frequency extension below 100 Hz is conditional on having measured element and junction data; simplified method has a restricted application field.
sources.applicability: Shows why a model cannot be responsibly populated from this brief's absent construction details. It is an airborne between-room model, not a measured finding.

sources.title: Hopkins & Turner, Field measurement of airborne sound insulation between rooms with non-diffuse sound fields at low frequencies
sources.version_or_commit: Applied Acoustics 66(12), 1339–1382, published 2005-12; DOI 10.1016/j.apacoust.2005.04.005. Publisher abstract only; full text access not obtained.
sources.locator: Publisher abstract/introduction/conclusion exposed in the ScienceDirect result; study proposes corner and central positions, 50/63/80 Hz one-third-octave protocol.
sources.observed_operation: Proposes corner plus central microphone locations to estimate room-average airborne sound levels at 50, 63, and 80 Hz with improved repeatability in non-diffuse small rooms.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Airborne insulation between small rooms; repeatability is same operator/short time, while reproducibility across days/operators was outside that study's scope. Not a complaint-event metric.
sources.applicability: Motivates multiple repeatable room positions and a low-frequency band check if the borrowed instrument supports them; does not establish this building's modes.

sources.title: FHWA-HEP-18-065, Measurement of Highway-Related Noise
sources.version_or_commit: FHWA manual report number HEP-18-065 (2018); current public HTML page viewed. The page does not expose a later revision date in the inspected sections.
sources.locator: Sections 4.6/background correction (lines 1400–1436), 7.0 groundborne vibration/noise (1843–1862), and 17.2 transducers (3264–3277).
sources.observed_operation: Explains field documentation, background adjustment, attached vibration transducers, coexistence of groundborne and airborne sound, and difficulty distinguishing path contributions from indoor SPL alone.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Highway-noise procedures and numerical examples are transportation-specific; do not transfer their noise limits or pass/fail rules to this project. The physical measurement caveat about co-occurring paths is relevant.
sources.applicability: Primary government measurement guidance for planning paired sound/vibration channels, background windows, fixed microphone metadata, and field notes; not a regulatory criterion for rehearsal music.

sources.title: Emslie & Hanson, Design and Acoustic Performance of a Drum Practice Music Studio
sources.version_or_commit: Australian Acoustical Society Acoustics 2008 proceedings paper AAS2008-64, presented 24–26 Nov 2008; explicitly marked not peer reviewed. A journal version exists, but this source ID is the proceedings copy.
sources.locator: PDF pages 1–2 baseline/constraints, 3–5 isolation/details and staged treatments, 6–8 facade/reverberation/boundary outcome.
sources.observed_operation: Reports baseline at two boundaries, construction of an isolated drum studio in a new garage extension, staged internal absorption, later exterior drumming levels, and separate internal family-room levels. Initial heavy masonry concept was rejected after slab-capacity concerns; roof performance later limited the facade; seal, penetration, gap, and vibration-bridge detailing demanded inspection.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Single Australian residential property, drum/cymbal source, nighttime measurement with low traffic background, local consent target and specific mic locations; unreviewed conference proceeding. Values are not general targets.
sources.applicability: Comparable only as a documented drum-neighbor implementation and a source of investigable detail/history; differs from shared rehearsal rooms and unknown construction, and includes a permanent build outside this assignment boundary.

sources.title: Gjers, Vibration and Airborne Sound in Repurposed Buildings: A Case Study of a Drum Kit in a Music Classroom
sources.version_or_commit: Australian Acoustical Society Proceedings of Acoustics 2024, paper 36, 6–8 Nov 2024.
sources.locator: PDF pages 1–5 setting/test setup, pp. 6–9 airborne and vibration findings and further-investigation limitations.
sources.observed_operation: A school music classroom in a commercial building was assessed over 180 mm and 450 mm concrete slab zones. Paired source/receiver meters and accelerometers were used; a 24 kg subset of kit on a 15 kg platform with nine 25 mm Sylomer SR11 pads was tested. The 180 mm Dw comparison changed by 5 dB; locations/contact points and some source comparisons differed. Frequency bands include both amplification and reduction; the authors state path separation is complex and further tests needed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: One site, specific slab zones, restricted component set/platform size, short steady-intensity play, time-limited two accelerometer positions; not a courtyard/outdoor test and not a clean generalizable product guarantee.
sources.applicability: Useful hypothesis and method comparator if source-to-floor coupling is suspected; reinforces need to control source/location and measure structural response, but cannot predict a result here.

sources.title: Shearer, Dance, Gomez-Agustina & Randell, Flexible control of acoustic conditions in a music rehearsal space using airbeds
sources.version_or_commit: Applied Acoustics 173, article 107708; published Feb 2021; DOI 10.1016/j.apacoust.2020.107708; peer-reviewed article; LSBU page identifies CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
sources.locator: LSBU institutional record abstract and bibliographic record, lines 18–34 and 46–50.
sources.observed_operation: Airbeds were tested in a university reverberation chamber, promising model selected and inflation dependence evaluated, then hall room-acoustic measurements before and after installation showed reduced low-frequency reverberation time in Henry Wood Hall.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Flexible low-frequency room conditioning for smaller ensembles/voice in a former church orchestral hall; the abstract does not provide product model or measured band values. It does not measure façade isolation or courtyard sound.
sources.applicability: Unfamiliar reversible room-acoustics alternative; worth investigating for in-room response only, not a neighbor noise-control prediction.

sources.title: Song & Kang, Effects of the absorber location on low-frequency noise control in typical dwelling layouts
sources.version_or_commit: Applied Acoustics 186 (2022), article 108465, DOI 10.1016/j.apacoust.2021.108465; UCL record provides the author-accepted manuscript link.
sources.locator: UCL Discovery abstract/record, lines 28–46; manuscript is offered as accepted version. A later repeat fetch of the PDF timed out, so evidence used here is limited to the record/abstract.
sources.observed_operation: Authors report in-situ steady-state measurements across coupled dwelling room layouts; absorber area and location changed low-frequency noise reduction and the loud/quiet spread, with diminishing gains or over-damping as area grew.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Typical dwelling topologies and steady-state source, not this unknown rehearsal building or an outdoor microphone result; abstract-only claims kept at that scope.
sources.applicability: Supports controlled testing of existing panel position and multiple room points, while explicitly not supporting external courtyard benefit.

sources.title: Getzner Sylomer SR 11 data sheet
sources.version_or_commit: Manufacturer data sheet, copyright/footer revision 04-2025; URL parameter v=6. Manufacturer says subject to change without notice.
sources.locator: Official manufacturer PDF, pp. 1–4: product characteristics and range of use (lines 0–42), measurement/load test conditions (60–72), curves (pp. 2–3), disclaimer/revision footer (173–177, 229).
sources.observed_operation: Reports load-deflection and vibration/isolation characteristics for SR11. Values shown apply to shape factor 3; static/dynamic load ranges and deflection differ; elasticity depends on frequency, specific load, and amplitude.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Manufacturer-data-sheet values are guidance subject to manufacturing tolerances and not guaranteed; do not equate them to guaranteed courtyard attenuation or select pad size without actual load/frequency/support conditions.
sources.applicability: Only a candidate to examine for a reversible, correctly sized source-to-structure test if vibration evidence appears; no product purchase or installation is recommended from this desk research.
